doc.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025

chapter: The Four Seasons and Bob Crewe
title: Buddy Saltzman's prediction and ten dollars per arrangement
summary: He wrote the Big Girls Don't Cry album arrangements for ten dollars each, replacing another arranger by working cheaper.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So then obviously when The Four Seasons became successful I became the arranger which gave me opportunity, and then my name was on records. And making a Four Seasons record, one of the – the drummer, Buddy Saltzman, who played on pretty much all The Four Seasons’ hits, said to me, “Charlie,” he said, “there’s going to be four stages to your career.” He said: Who’s Charlie Calello? We have to get Charlie Calello. What we need is a young Charlie Calello. And whatever happened to Charlie Calello.
Well I’m glad to have you here. Here’s what happened. That’s terrific. Was there a point where you said, “Hmm, I should be getting paid for this, and how much, and how do I charge?”
Well I wrote the arrangements to the “Big Girls Don’t Cry” album for ten bucks apiece.
And you don’t ever get any licensing or royalties for that, is that correct?

No, later on as a producer I did but I was pleased to, you know, to get paid. Because I was writing arrangements for nothing. And there were a couple of interesting things about it. Bob was using another arranger, but he found out that not only I could do the same job but I could work cheaper, which I didn’t know about. Then I found out that I should really ask him for more money because I was overloaded with stuff and it was starting to become a real job.
